Management won’t see your name, your account or the exact time. What you write or photograph may still show who you are. It goes out a few minutes after you send it and reaches them at the end of that hour.

An anonymous report goes through the app with no login attached. Your company sees “Anonymous” and only the hour it was sent — never your name, your account or the exact time — and nothing stored with the report links it to you. For your privacy it leaves this phone on its own a few minutes after the app’s other traffic (usually within 15 minutes while the app is open), and reaches management at the end of that hour. Management can reply in the app; you read replies in My Management Reports and stay anonymous. What is still true: the app’s hosting service (Supabase) keeps request logs for 1 to 7 days — the internet address, the phone and browser type, and the time of every request. Only the app owner can see those logs, and with them could match an anonymous request to this phone. What you write, and what your photos show, can also give you away. Your phone keeps your own copy and the secret key for reading replies.
Management also sees the email you sign in with.
<1>Reports aren’t an emergency line. For anything urgent, call.</1>Sent means your company’s inbox has it, not that a manager has read it or acted on it.

Send Report sends it to your company’s management through the app — no email. The To line above shows where it goes. It is saved on this phone first; with no signal it waits here and goes by itself, and the app never says Sent until the server has it.
No one to send it to yet? Save Without Sending keeps it in your Records marked Not sent. Nothing is sent; it’s listed under Saved, not sent in My Management Reports, where you can send it later.
A copy of what you send is kept in your own Records — even anonymous ones — so you have a record of what you reported and when.
